summary: An exec gate that says not yet checks again after 5 s, doubling up to every 30 s, instead of after 1 min doubling up to every 15 min

replay.detail: No claim, projection or replay change; gate results keep their shape and check numbers.

schema.detail: No table, index or migration change.

compatibility.detail: Recheck waits after not yet are 5, 10, 20, then 30 s (were 60, 120, 240, 480, then 900 s). An exec gate answers about state the graph does not observe (a host-deploy admit gate waiting for a remote host to go idle measured 129 s of dead time after the condition held), so its recheck cap is the longest a gate that now holds waits unseen. A long-waiting gate runs its check up to 2 times a minute instead of 4 times an hour; each check is one supervised exec plus the pass that records it. Conditions the graph observes should use field or exists gates, which a change wakes at once.

downtime.detail: No restart or migration beyond a normal deploy.

manual.detail: No operator action is required. A gate whose check is expensive should do its own caching, or move the observation into a resource that a field gate reads.

recovery.detail: A gate already waiting is judged against the new schedule at its next evaluation, which a pass or a change triggers; its armed timer can still fire at the old time.
